# The Four Corners <span class="script">四句</span>

<p class="lens-meta"><code class="lens-code">FOUR-CORNERS</code> · Buddhist — Madhyamaka and Dignāgan logic · <strong>Enforced — owns a gate</strong></p>

## The failure it names

collapsing a contested question into a binary before the other positions have been stated

## What it does

a contested claim must address all four corners: A, ¬A, both, neither

## Enforced gates

These block a citation packet deterministically — no model in the loop:

- `PEIR-CORNERS-UNADDRESSED`

## Worked example

"Is light a wave or a particle?" forces two corners, and each is wrong alone — the physics needed the third: it is both. 四句 keeps all four (is, is-not, both, neither) open until the question earns a collapse.

## Sources

- Nāgārjuna, Mūlamadhyamakakārikā 1.1, 18.8
- <https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/nagarjuna/>
